title: The Spiral Structure Model: A Geometric Phenomenology of Wave-Particle Duality, Spin, and Electromagnetic Coupling
content: We present the Spiral Structure Model (SSM), a phenomenological model in the tradition of Bohr's atomic theory: deliberately restricted to kinematics and geometry, it trades computational depth for ontological clarity and exposes its predictions to direct experimental disproof. Three postulates suffice: (I) the photon is a pointlike energy quantum moving on a helical worldline whose axial (signal) speed and azimuthal (tangential) speed both equal c; (II) physical space is an elastic, relativistically covariant medium sustaining vortex excitations; (III) the electron is a stable topological vortex defect of that medium. From these we obtain, with the logical status of every step labeled: the photon's intrinsic angular momentum mc rγ = ℏ as a conditional geometric theorem, anchored in the classical wave identity L = E/ω; a logarithmic vortex self-energy that confines the helical quantum in a genuine stable minimum with zero free parameters; a geometric reason for the two polarization states and the absence of a longitudinal mode; the 720-degree periodicity of the electron, anchored in the homotopy π1(SO(3)) = Z2, yielding spin ℏ/2; the fine-structure constant as a ratio of structural scales, α = re/a0; a phase-coupling account of two-slit interference; a double-helix ontology of entangled pairs reproducing the CHSH value S = 2√2; and two falsifiable discriminants, namely an intrinsic photonic dark core locked to the wavelength and independent of numerical aperture, and a spin-dependent electron form-factor window at momentum transfers near mc. The geometric uncertainty estimate is shown to saturate the Heisenberg bound exactly, Δx·Δp = ℏ/2; the sub-Heisenberg estimate (√2 − 1)ℏ reported in earlier versions is withdrawn as a category error that confused a systematic offset with a statistical width. Three components of the framework in its earlier form are tested against their own criteria and removed: a power-law confinement ansatz that furnished no stable equilibrium (Sec. 3.1), the 0.414ℏ uncertainty estimate (Sec. 3.5), and a static strong-field regularization ansatz excluded by heavy-ion spectroscopy (Sec. 6). The framework does not compete with quantum electrodynamics in precision; it offers a coherent and experimentally vulnerable geometric picture of the quantum.
